description: Open firmware for the Echo Show 5, 1st and 2nd gen: Alpine Linux instead of Android, no Alexa. A local Home Assistant voice satellite with its own touch screen, on-device wake word, SSH and A/B over-the-air updates.

latest_release.name: v1.6.40
latest_release.body:
The rest of the screen and setup page refresh, contributors' work on pop-ups, volume and translations, and fixes from your reports.

- **Louder 2nd gen Shows**: the Echo Show 5 and Show 8 2nd gen now use the volume curve Fire OS used, read from the unit itself, so full volume is about as loud as it was on Fire OS. **The same volume step is louder than before** from about step 10 up, for music, alarms and replies alike: turn down after updating if it's too much. Thanks, nuno407 (#546).
- **Pop-ups**: a calendar pop-up tapped away on one Show now goes away on the other Shows in the house too. Thanks, Uthrom (#558).
- **Bluetooth speakers**: the Echo's volume now sets the speaker's own volume (absolute volume), so the top step is the speaker's top, the speaker's buttons change the Echo's volume, and a speaker that was switched off no longer comes back quiet. Speakers without absolute volume work as before. Thanks to shawnsi for the report (#550).
- **Snapcast**: the volume follows snapclient's own curve, so a TECHO5 device is no longer much quieter than the rest of its group at low volume. Thanks, Orestos (#561).
- **Clock**: the Classic clock drifts a few pixels over time, so it doesn't leave a shadow of the digits on the panel. Thanks to redblack2412 for the report (#560).
- **Names**: devices with letters like ü in their names show correctly in the call list, and calling or Dropping In on them by name works. Thanks to Tobi-IT for the report (#557).
- **Drawn dashboard**: the screen and the setup page say where the Home Assistant token comes from and show the action to run. Thanks to doctorwho68 for the report (#551).
- **Streamed dashboard**: the Home Assistant header no longer flashes when a dashboard comes back after the screen was off. Update the dashcast container to the image released with this version. Thanks to mauricekft for the report (techo5-spot#12).
- **Screen**: a press shows only where a tap acts, now also on the clock page, the calendar, the media, color, thermostat and fan sheets and the music library; the weather page fills its forecast boxes and uses the room on larger screens; calendar events are at least a line tall; dark custom themes get readable accents; the camera grid's title and hint have room at larger text sizes; a camera or dashboard that can't connect shows a short message, with the details in the log.
- **Skylight**: a 150% text size; the calendar's month and week stay at 125% there, where their events keep their words.
- **Words**: Dutch now covers nearly the whole screen. Thanks, christianschmidt (#538). The reset row is translated in every language. Thanks, royto (#556). The last English words on the screen (the calendar pop-up, reminders, radio notes, clock style names, Next) follow the screen's language.
- **Setup page**: the tabs are regrouped into Status, Alarms & Timers, Sound, Voice, Screen, Cameras, Network, Privacy and System, and old links still open the right place; Status also shows the next alarm, running timers and Tailscale or NetBird; a refused form comes back with what you typed (passwords left out); an alarm's form saves all of it or nothing.
- **Logs**: what Music Assistant refuses (#521), what a voice request sent up (#477) and what each wake word scored during a call (#484) are logged for diagnostics. Thanks, new-res and rabacen.

Please open an issue if something doesn't work.

detail.readme:
Your Echo Show, rebuilt. Linux inside, Home Assistant in charge, no Amazon cloud.

What's new · Built on EchoLocal · Why · Screenshots · Stock vs TECHO5 · Install · Under the hood · Credits · TECHO5 ATHENA · TECHO5 Dot · TECHO5 Spot

--- > **New: the Echo Show 8 2nd gen (2021, `athena`) runs TECHO5 on a 64-bit mainline Linux kernel.** > The story, the board and the UART pads: [TECHO5 ATHENA](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-athena). > Install: [docs/install-athena.md](docs/install-athena.md). **TECHO5** (Tech Echo 5) is open firmware for **Amazon's Echo Show 5 and Echo Show 8**, both generations of each. It replaces Fire OS and Alexa with a small Alpine Linux image and one Go daemon, turning the Show into a fast, private Home Assistant voice satellite with a touch screen of its own. It started on the Show 5, which is where the name comes from. **Every Echo that can be unlocked now runs it.** The bootloader exploit these devices are opened with, [amonet](https://github.com/R0rt1z2/amonet), opens most of these Echos, and saiyaku-athena unlocks the Show 8 2nd gen. All of them run the same daemon: | Device | Model | Repository | Status | |---|---|---|---| | **Echo Show 5, 2nd gen** (2021, `cronos`) | C76N8S | this one | In daily use | | **Echo Show 5, 1st gen** (2019, `checkers`) | H23K37 | this one, same binary; hardware notes in [techo5-checkers](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-checkers) | In daily use | | **Echo Show 8, 1st gen** (2019, `crown`) | C7H6N3 | this one, same binary | In daily use | | **Echo Show 8, 2nd gen** (2021, `athena`) | A8H3N2 | this one, same daemon on its own 64-bit mainline kernel; the story in [TECHO5 ATHENA](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-athena) | In daily use on two units | | **Echo Spot, 1st gen** (2017, `rook`) | VN94DQ | [TECHO5 Spot](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-spot) | In daily use | | **Echo Dot, 2nd gen** (2016, `biscuit`) | RS03QR | [TECHO5 Dot](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot) | In daily use | | **Echo, 2nd gen** (2017, `radar`) | XC56PY | [TECHO5 Dot](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot#echo-2nd-gen), same release and daemon | Working on one unit | | **Echo Dot, 3rd gen** (2018, `donut`) | D9N29T | [TECHO5 Dot](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot#echo-dot-3rd-gen), same release, its own daemon build | Working on two units | | **Echo Input** (2018, `cupcake`) | C1125P | [TECHO5 Dot](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot#echo-input), the Echo Dot 3rd gen's release and daemon build | Experimental, not yet tried on a unit | | **Android tablets and the Meta Portal**, no unlock | Android 8.0 or later, ARM | [TECHO5 Panel](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-panel), an app with the same daemon inside ([docs/panel.md](docs/panel.md)) | Tested on a Fire HD 8 (10th gen), a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite and a Meta Portal (2nd gen); other tablets may work | Every other device amonet opens is a Fire tablet. No Echo made after 2021 has a public unlock. Beyond the Echos and the Panel's tablets, the **Skylight Calendar 15** (150-CAL) runs it too, a wall calendar with a 1920x1080 touch screen. TECHO5 puts its own 64-bit mainline kernel and the same daemon on it, over adb, after a full backup. It has no microphone, so it's a screen and a speaker: no wake word, voice, phone calls or intercom. Tried on one unit, the newest port: [docs/install-skylight.md](docs/install-skylight.md). How it compares with EchoLocal, EchoMuse, echo-dot-assist, Kiosk Satellite and View Assist: [docs/comparison.md](docs/comparison.md).

Waking to light. For up to half an hour before an alarm the screen becomes a dawn, on a curve that does most of its work near the end. Every frame here is drawn by the code the device draws with.

## What's new The bigger changes of September to November 2026. Every release lists the rest. - 📞 **Call by wake word, Hang up bar, repeating alarms** (v1.6.28). A wake word can call a phone book contact ([#463](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/463)), calls can keep the page on screen with a Hang up bar ([#459](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/459)), and the Set an alarm blueprint understands repeating days ([#461](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/461)). - 🎙️ **External microphone processing and custom screens** (v1.6.27). An interface for a separately installed audio processing helper, off unless you choose External ([#407](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/407), [docs/external-asp.md](docs/external-asp.md)). Other boards can add their own full-screen pages and show one when idle ([#447](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/447)). AirPlay 2 works on the Show 8 2nd gen ([techo5-athena #5](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-athena/issues/5)). - 🎶 **Snapcast, your own Headscale and a dark nursery** (v1.6.26). Every device can be a [Snapcast](https://github.com/snapcast/snapcast) client, in step with the house's other Snapcast speakers ([#406](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/406)). Tailscale can join a [Headscale](https://headscale.net) server you run instead of Tailscale's, from the setup page or the `headscale_login` action ([docs/tailscale.md](docs/tailscale.md#your-own-headscale)). **Baby monitor light** turns the listening mark down to its dimmest or off, for a nursery kept dark ([#448](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/448)). - 📝 **To-do lists, a baby monitor and your own sounds** (v1.6.23). With echo cancellation on, you can speak right after the wake word, without waiting for the sound. A **To-do** tab in the drawer shows Home Assistant's to-do and shopping lists on the Show, the Skylight and the Panel. A private link plays the room's sound live in a phone's browser (**Baby monitor**, off until you turn it on), and the wake, volume, button, Bluetooth and Drop In sounds can be your own. **Voice volume** and **Call volume** sit beside the music volume, and the assistant's replies can play on another speaker. Pop-ups can be large or huge for reading across a room ([#396](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/396)), the night clock can keep Next up ([#397](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/397)), and a fan on a drawn dashboard opens speed, direction and presets on a long press ([#410](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/410)). The Echo Dot and Echo 2nd gen get a ring that follows the music, and all of them a **Clearer speech** switch. Bluetooth devices such as Hue bulbs can be paired through the proxy ([#398](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/398)), the Show 8 2nd gen uses the ondemand CPU governor ([#413](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/413)), and the installers try a failed download again ([#393](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/393)). - 🌧️ **Rain on the glass, and a news update by voice** (v1.6.22). Rain on the weather page and the weather art gathers on the glass and runs down, and lightning strikes at random with a new bolt each time. The direct assistant plays a news update when asked. **Wi-Fi quiet hours** keeps the device off the Wi-Fi at night ([#391](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/391)), and a repeating alarm can skip one morning from its wake-up light ([#360](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/360)). - 📊 **Wake scores, a privacy switch and new diagnostics** (v1.6.21). Voice request events carry the wake word's score and why a request was canceled ([#381](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/381)), and **Send voice text** keeps what you say out of Home Assistant ([#383](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/383)). New sensors show CPU usage, wake word load and the last boot reason ([#386](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/386)). The Show 8 2nd gen gets an opt-in boot layer that falls back to the other slot by itself ([#340](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/340)). - ⏸️ **A longer pause before the device stops listening** (v1.6.20). **End of speech pause** sets how long a pause ends what you say, from 0.6 to 2 seconds, for anyone who stops to think mid-sentence ([#374](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/374)). Clearing Music Assistant's queue now clears Now Playing at once ([#150](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/150)), and a Tessera "go to page" tile opens its page ([#376](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/376)). - 👏 **A stricter clap, and "Alexa, stop" over a ring** (v1.6.19). **Clap sensitivity** adds a Strict choice for a room where a desk passes for a double clap, and the clap event carries what it measured ([#373](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/373)). A wake word nearly heard over a ringing timer pauses the ring for the second try ([#372](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/372)), and smaller **Calendar chips** fit a long list of calendars ([#371](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/371)). - 🌍 **Galician, and a Monday week** (v1.6.18). **Screen language** gains Galician, with its own voice words and dates ([#368](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/368)), and Dutch for the labels and buttons ([#365](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/365)). A **Week starts Monday** calendar switch, off by default ([#369](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/369)), and a wake word threshold of its own for while the speaker plays ([#367](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/367)). - 🔠 **Text size and a dashboard layout** (v1.6.17). A **Text size** setting draws every word on the screen from 70% to 125% ([#363](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/363)), and **Brightness** steps down to 5% for a dark room ([#362](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/362)). Drawn dashboards wrap long tile names ([#357](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/357)), show a dimmer's level as a bar ([#358](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/358)), offer a *Name below* tile layout, and drop the room from a name under its room's heading. AirPlay 2 over IPv6 now really plays ([#343](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/343)), and a third Show 8 2nd gen screen is tested ([#361](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/361)). - 🎙️ **Record takes of a word** (v1.6.16). The setup page can record takes of a wake word on the device's own microphones, after a press at the device, and hand them over as a zip for training ([#315](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/315)). AirPlay 2 plays from a Mac or iPhone that connects over IPv6 ([#343](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/343)), Now Playing goes once Music Assistant's queue is emptied ([#150](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/150)), and more of the screen follows **Screen language**, with a [translation status page](docs/translating.md). - 🌍 **French and Turkish on the screen** (v1.6.15). **Screen language** gains French ([#346](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/346)) and Turkish ([#349](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/349)). Every alarm can be turned off at once for a trip, and Home Assistant gets a Next scheduled alarm sensor ([#350](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/discussions/350)). A wake word sent from the setup page scores on the features it was trained on ([#352](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/352)). - 📖 **Long answers page along with the voice** (v1.6.14). An Assist answer too long for the screen is shown a page at a time, turning as the voice reads it, on the Show and the Spot ([#333](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/discussions/333)). The glance chips under the clock can keep one size ([#332](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/332)), and a second AirPlay sender can take over from the first ([#334](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/334)). - 🌍 **German, Spanish and Italian on the screen** (v1.6.13). **Screen language** gains German ([#322](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/322)), Spanish ([#327](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/327)) and a first Italian draft ([#310](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/310)), and the PIN pad and alarm editor follow the language too. The 2nd gen Show 8's camera pages and stream use its hardware JPEG encoder ([#320](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/320), [#321](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/321)), and calls can switch to WebRTC's echo canceller for their length ([#331](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/331)). - 📡 **The Panel is a Bluetooth proxy, and AirPlay can set the volume** (v1.6.12). On TECHO5 Panel, Android's Bluetooth now feeds Home Assistant's Bluetooth proxy, with one active connection lent through it ([#278](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/278)); the Panel app also bridges the front camera and, on the JBL Link View, the raw microphone. On the Echos, **AirPlay sets the volume** makes an iPhone's or Mac's AirPlay slider the device's own volume ([#312](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/312)), and Home Assistant can turn an alarm off and back on without deleting it (`alarm_turn_off` / `alarm_turn_on`, [#317](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/317)). - 🖥️ **The 2nd gen Show 8 draws its screen on its GPU** (v1.6.11). The Show 8 2nd gen's Mali GPU now draws the panel, which leaves the cores free, and an **Adaptive backlight** switch turns the backlight down on dark screens and draws the pixels brighter by as much, so the screen looks the same for less light ([#308](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/308)). Its camera no longer hangs on a picture too big for the encoder's buffer ([#309](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/309)). Also in v1.6.11: the **Bluetooth Secure Connections** switch now really reaches the controller ([#183](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/183)), and the installers say when a unit restarts partway, what was erased and how to finish by hand. - 🎚️ **Wake word scores, and wakesmith for words of your own** (v1.6.10). The setup page shows each wake word's score as it comes, so you can see how close a word gets in your room and pick a threshold that fits ([#314](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/314)). To train a word of your own, [wakesmith](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/wakesmith) does it on your own computer from synthetic speech plus real voices: takes you record in the browser and the clips your devices kept. [Training a wake word](#training-a-wake-word-of-your-own) - 🎵 **Now Playing follows several players** (v1.6.10). Pick more than one media player, and the screen shows whichever is playing. Also in v1.6.10: the 2nd gen Show 8's JD9365 backlight comes back from off ([#253](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/253)), reminders speak on a Home Assistant that isn't in English ([#294](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/294)), and Bluetooth proxy connections need an API encryption key. - 🇯🇵 **Japanese, Louder speech and Dim after idle** (v1.6.9). The screen in Japanese ([#270](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/270)), AirPlay 2 groups that play in step ([#311](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/311)), a **Louder speech** switch for replies and announcements, **Dim after idle**, and four new skins. - 🎵 **AirPlay 2 on every device** (v1.6.8). With the AirPlay switch on, an iPhone can group the device with other AirPlay 2 speakers, like a HomePod or a Sonos. The **AirPlay 2** switch keeps it to classic AirPlay if a group doesn't play in step. Its firewall ports are open only while the AirPlay 2 receiver runs. - 🛰️ **NetBird** (v1.6.8). The other way, beside Tailscale, to keep a device in another house in your Home Assistant, with NetBird's own service or your own server. Off until you give it a setup key. [docs/netbird.md](docs/netbird.md) - 📶 **Also in v1.6.8.** Home Assistant can connect to Bluetooth devices through a Show, up to three at a time, with the new **Bluetooth proxy connections** switch ([#184](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/184)). Weekend nights can have their own hours ([#305](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/305)), and the Skylight's night clock now dims well below its old floor. - 🌐 **Reach a device from away** (v1.6.7). An Echo Show, Echo Spot or Skylight can join your Tailscale network, so a device in another house stays in your own Home Assistant, and its setup page can be opened from afar with Remote setup. Off until you give it a key; over the tailnet only Home Assistant's encrypted connection, the setup page while Remote setup is on, and SSH when it's on get in. [docs/tailscale.md](docs/tailscale.md) - 🆕 **The Skylight Calendar 15** (v1.3.0). Not an Echo: the 15-inch wall calendar (150-CAL) runs TECHO5 on its own 64-bit mainline Linux kernel. Touch, the calendar, photos, dashboards, music and the radio, Bluetooth, the light sensor and the clock work. It has no microphone, so there's no wake word or voice, and no phone calls or intercom. One command installs it over adb from its stock firmware, after a full backup of the unit; it has been tried on one unit. Install: [docs/install-skylight.md](docs/install-skylight.md) - 📱 **TECHO5 on a tablet, no unlock** (v1.3.0). TECHO5 Panel is an Android app with the same daemon inside: Home Assistant adds it like an Echo, with the same wake words, screens, timers, alarms, intercom and announcements. No unlock and no root, on tablets and the Meta Portal. Tested on a Fire HD 8 (10th gen), a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite and a Meta Portal (2nd gen); other Android 8.0+ tablets may work. [TECHO5 Panel](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-panel), [docs/panel.md](docs/panel.md) - 🗣️ **Also in v1.3.0.** Nearest device answers is now on by default, also on devices where it had been turned off. The Show 8 (both generations) draws some controls larger to fit its screen. The Show 8 2nd gen's kernel now picks its screen from the name the bootloader passes, so a unit installed with `--force-panel` gets its own screen's driver with the kernel update (ten screens known; only the BOE ILI9881C one tried on a unit; three tried since v1.6.17). - 📷 **The Echo Show 8 2nd gen's camera works** (v1.2.24). Live on its own screen, a Home Assistant camera, and everything else the other Shows do with theirs (presence, person detection, gestures, your recorder). It's off while the device is muted or the shutter is closed. It comes with a new kernel, which the device installs on its own as a trial and puts back if it doesn't come up right. Also: a **Bluetooth Secure Connections** switch for phones that pair and then drop a second later ([#183](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/183)); on the Dot, AirPlay recovers when it stops showing up after the first use ([techo5-dot#14](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot/issues/14)); and the camera's `/camera.jpg` and `/camera.mjpeg` pages now ask for the camera password and light the green dot while they're watched. **If something reads those pages with no password today** (a Home Assistant Generic Camera, a recorder), set a camera password and give it to that with Digest authentication, or it stops getting pictures. [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md#4-cameras) - 📅 **A calendar for the wall** (v1.2.23). The calendar's new look: a day and a week on their hours, a cleaner month, Coming up with each day's weather, event icons, countdowns, a filter for which calendars a screen shows, and the next event at the foot of the clock, each with its own switch under Settings > Display > Calendar. The screen can stay on when you say "lights off" in its room ([#179](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/179)), light themes work over a photo, and the Show's music buttons are drawn like the rest of its buttons ([#173](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/173)). Music Assistant finds a device it reaches by address again after the device restarts ([#182](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/182)), a radio favorite Home Assistant didn't start says why on the screen ([#174](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/174)), a slideshow folder set again is read again at once ([#180](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/180)), and the log says why the ambient noise sensor has no reading ([#178](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/178)). Thanks to [@christianschmidt](https://github.com/christianschmidt) and [@tibole](https://github.com/tibole). [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md#calendar) - 🔗 **Settings that follow you, a realtime voice, and a camera that knows a person** (v1.2.22). Pick a setting on the setup page and tick the other devices that should keep it in step: each one agrees first, and a device that was off catches up when it's back. A wake word can be answered by a speech-to-speech model at OpenAI, xAI or Gemini (it sends your voice to them, and they bill for it; off until you choose it, with a daily limit). With presence detection on, a Show or Spot can tell a person from anything else that moves, on the device. - 🎥 **Your Echo as a camera for your recorder, and cameras by the grid** (v1.2.21). A Show or Spot can serve its own camera to Frigate or any NVR over RTSP and ONVIF, with a login and a green dot on the screen while it's watched; the Show shows up to six cameras at once, and go2rtc's streams join the list. Off until you turn them on. - 🗣️ **The nearest Echo answers, and more you can run from home** (v1.2.21). With several devices in earshot, only the one that heard you best answers. Thermostats open their controls in Drawn mode ([#170](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/issues/170)); settings save to a file and restore; a signed remote API and live logs; timers pause and take extra time from Home Assistant; and an event on two calendars shows once. Thanks to [@remylpat](https://github.com/remylpat), and to [@wonderslug](https://github.com/wonderslug) for the Echo 2nd gen's own speaker tuning ([#169](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/pull/169)). - 🔊 **The Echo 2nd gen** (dot-v1.0.19). The 2017 Echo (`radar`) runs TECHO5 Dot: the same release, installer and daemon as the Dot, with its own amplifier, the speaker filters from the unit itself and its own Bluetooth kernel. Its USB is only inside the case: [install steps](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-dot#echo-2nd-gen). - 🌄 **Light only alarms, and a night that's easier to live with** (v1.2.20). Drawn on the device: instant, no server Streamed: exactly as Home Assistant draws it
**Home Assistant dashboards on the screen** (v0.9.0). The Echo Show and the Echo Spot can show a dashboard as a page you swipe in from the left edge of the clock (on the Spot, from the ring menu), or in place of the clock when nothing else is on the screen. There are two ways, picked per device in Home Assistant: - **Drawn on the device.** The device reads the dashboard's cards and draws them itself, in your theme's colors: tiles you can tap or slide for brightness, position and temperature, rows with switches, graphs, gauges, pictures and more. Taps are instant and nothing else is needed. With no dashboard picked, it builds a Rooms dashboard from your Home Assistant areas. - **Streamed.** [dashcast](dashcast/README.md), a small server that runs next to Home Assistant (a Docker image for PCs and Raspberry Pis), opens the dashboard in a headless browser and sends the screen only what changes, encrypted with a key of your choosing. It looks exactly as Home Assistant draws it, custom cards included, and it can show built-in pages like Energy and History. For a Show on a wall, a tap on the clock can open the dashboard, a few tiles can fill the whole screen, and the clock comes back on its own after the time you choose. Which to use, how to set it up and what each can do: **[docs/dashboards.md](docs/dashboards.md)**.

[Screenshots](docs/screenshots/README.md#echo-show-8) ## Built on EchoLocal TECHO5 started from **[EchoLocal](https://github.com/ygelfand/echolocal)** by Yuri Gelfand (MIT), which already turns the Echo Dot 2 (`biscuit`, the same MT8163 family) into an ESPHome-native Home Assistant satellite, with a single static Go daemon that drives the hardware directly. TECHO5's `echod` is that daemon, vendored and ported to the Show 5's `cronos`, and much of it is still EchoLocal's code: the wake word engine, the ALSA client and the service framework almost unchanged, and the voice satellite, media player and component registry grown from EchoLocal's own. What TECHO5 added is the Show's hardware, the screen, the camera, Bluetooth, the update and slot system, phone calls, and a minimal Alpine root filesystem in place of Android. See [NOTICE](NOTICE) for the full attribution and EchoLocal's license. ## Why TECHO5 | | | |---|---| | 🐧 **Real Linux, no Android** | The Show boots straight into a minimal Alpine Linux root filesystem. No Android framework, no Google services, no app store: one daemon drives the microphones, speaker, screen, camera and radios directly. | | 🚫 **No Alexa, no Amazon account, no Amazon cloud** | Your voice goes only to *your* Home Assistant, over its encrypted ESPHome API. The Show reaches the internet just for what you use: update checks against this repo, network time, radio streams with their song and cover lookups, the rain radar map, and in the U.S. the National Weather Service's weather alerts. Voice and control keep working with the internet down, as long as your Home Assistant pipeline is local. | | 🎙️ **Two wake words, two assistants** | microWakeWord runs on the device and listens for two wake words at once, each with its own Home Assistant assistant: "Okay Nabu" for a local one and "Hey Jarvis" for a cloud one, say. Each has its own sensitivity, sounds, ring and follow-up. Twelve words come with it ("Alexa", "Okay Nabu", "Hey Jarvis", "Hey Mycroft", "Computer" and more), and you can add your own. Say "stop", with no wake word, to stop an alarm, an answer or the music. Echo cancellation keeps it listening over music. [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md#two-wake-words-two-assistants) | | 🧠 **Voice without Home Assistant, if you want** | Instead of Assist, the device can use your own speech servers (Wyoming: faster-whisper and Piper) and a chat model (llama.cpp, Ollama or anything OpenAI-style). It sets timers and alarms, plays the radio, the news update you ask for (Fox, NPR, ABC or your own) and Music Assistant, changes the volume and calls other devices, and can look things up with SearXNG. Or answer a wake word with a realtime voice at OpenAI, xAI or Gemini, with your own key. [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md#voice-without-home-assistant) | | 🔐 **Secure by default** | SSH is keys-only and off until you turn it on; keys arrive only through Home Assistant. The camera and screen web pages start closed, and a firewall lets in nothing on Wi-Fi but what the device serves. No password logins, not even in rescue. | | 🔄 **Updates that can't brick it** | Signed releases install over the air from Home Assistant's update card into the spare of two root filesystem slots, boot on trial, and fall back on their own if the new one doesn't settle. Follow the stable or the dev channel, and let it install on its own between 2 and 5 AM if you like. | | 📺 **A screen that's actually useful** | Clock and weather, the conversation as it happens, a glance strip of chips from Home Assistant along the foot of the clock, a calendar, now playing with song, cover art and lyrics, your Home Assistant dashboards, forecasts, a live rain radar, the National Weather Service's alerts (in the U.S.), live cameras from Home Assistant or go2rtc, up to six at once, notifications, timers and alarms, Wi-Fi setup, Home Assistant's to-do and shopping lists, 13 themes, ten fonts, ten languages (five with the whole screen translated, Spanish part of it, and Dutch, Portuguese and Russian the clock and weather), and 15 clock styles you swipe between. Home Assistant's to-do and shopping lists show on the Show's screen | ## How well does it hear? | Device | Mics | |---|:---:| | Echo Show 5, 1st and 2nd gen | 2 | | Echo Show 8, 1st and 2nd gen | 4 | | Echo Spot | 4 | | Echo Dot, 2nd gen | 7 | | Echo Dot, 3rd gen | 4 | | Echo, 2nd gen | 7 | The Dot's seven are a ring of six plus one in the middle, the best array of the bunch. The wake word runs on the device itself. After that, what you say goes to your Home Assistant pipeline, so misheard words are mostly down to the speech to text you have set up in HA, not the mics. There's echo cancellation too, so it can hear you over its own music. You can tune a lot of it from Home Assistant: **Microphone gain**, **Microphone mixing** (all averaged, center mic only, delay and sum, or beamformer), **Microphone noise reduction**, **Microphone echo cancellation** and the **Wake word threshold**. The defaults are what worked best in my testing, but every room is different. If the device's own models don't hear your voice well, Home Assistant's wake word engine (openWakeWord, say) can listen alongside it, or only check the wakes the device wasn't sure of: [Wake word on Home Assistant](docs/setup.md#wake-word-on-home-assistant). **Keep wake clips** saves what your room really says, so a model you train fits it: [Wake word clips](docs/setup.md#wake-word-clips). ### Training a wake word of your own For a word that isn't in the list, or one that hears your voice better, use **[wakesmith](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/wakesmith)**, our wake word trainer. It trains microWakeWord models (what TECHO5 runs) and openWakeWord models on your own computer, on an NVIDIA or Intel Arc GPU or the CPU alone, from a page in your browser. It mixes synthetic speech with real voices: takes you record in the browser, your device's saved [wake word clips](docs/setup.md#wake-word-clips), and Common Voice. Every model is scored on recordings it never trained on, so you can compare runs before you pick a cutoff. Load the result on the setup page like any other ([A wake word of your own](docs/setup.md#a-wake-word-of-your-own)), and the setup page's wake word scores show how it does in your room. [docs/training-wake-word.md](docs/training-wake-word.md) walks through it step by step, and the manual way with microWakeWord's own tools for a language other than English. On my Show 5 it hears me fine from across the room without raising my voice. With music playing I have to raise my voice, and sometimes still need to tap the screen or a button to get it to hear me. The standard Built-in microphone pipeline does not use Amazon's factory voice processing, so it's not going to match Alexa at its best. An optional [External ASP interface](docs/external-asp.md) allows a separately installed, compatible helper to process microphone audio instead. The standard installation needs no such helper. The built-in processing is a lot better than it was a month ago though, and still getting better. ## Install **New to this? Start with [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md)**: every step from a stock Echo Show 5, Dot or Spot, with the unlock guides linked, what to check after each step, and notes for Windows, Linux and macOS. Once it's in Home Assistant, **[Setting it up](docs/setup.md)** covers photos, weather, cameras, music and the night settings, in order. You need a Show 5 **unlocked and running LineageOS 18.1** — 2nd gen with [amonet-cronos](https://xdaforums.com/t/unlock-root-twrp-unbrick-amazon-echo-show-5-2nd-gen-2021-cronos.4772596/) and [this ROM](https://xdaforums.com/t/rom-unofficial-11-cronos-lineageos-18-1-for-the-amazon-echo-show-5-2021.4772598/) in its 2026-09-04 build (v0.4; the newer v0.5 is not supported yet), 1st gen with [amonet-checkers](https://xdaforums.com/t/unlock-root-twrp-unbrick-amazon-echo-show-5-1st-gen-2019-checkers.4762900/) and R0rt1z2's `checkers` build of the same LineageOS (v0.7) — a USB cable, a computer (Windows, Linux or macOS) with Python 3, `adb` and `fastboot`, and Home Assistant. Each [release](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5/releases/latest) carries everything else: the boot image (with Bluetooth) and the root filesystem. Nothing is built. ``` git clone https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5 cd techo5 python3 tools/install-show.py ``` It finds the Show, asks what to call it and asks once before erasing anything (or takes `--serial`, `--name` and `--force` from a script), downloads and checks the release, flashes the boot image, creates the slot store and installs over the USB serial console, and prints where the Home Assistant key is kept. Later updates come from Home Assistant. Every step by hand, and the fixes for what can go wrong: **[docs/install.md](docs/install.md)**. > **Status:** in daily use on at least five 2nd gen Echo Show 5s, a 1st gen Show 5, two 1st gen > Show 8s and two 2nd gen Show 8s, plus the Spot and the Dot, and working on an Echo 2nd gen, an > Echo Dot 3rd gen and a Skylight Calendar 15. It's a hobby project, not a product: keep your backups, and expect rough edges. **Echo Show 5 1st gen (2019, `checkers`)** installs with the same command: the installer sees which generation it is talking to and takes that unit's boot image from the release. Everything works on it: screen, touch, speaker, microphones, wake word, camera, the mute button and voice. One is in daily use. The hardware notes are in [techo5-checkers](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-checkers). **Echo Show 8 1st gen (2019, `crown`)** installs with the same command as well. Its screen, touch, speaker, four microphones, wake word, camera, lens cover and mute latch all work, and it takes slot updates like the others. Two of them are in daily use. Two things worth knowing first: a seller's model number does not tell the two Show 8 generations apart, so go by the year when buying second-hand. A unit installed before v1.0.1 needs the new boot image so a quick tap to unmute no longer leaves the camera off ([updating the boot image](docs/install.md#updating-the-boot-image)). **Echo Show 8 2nd gen (2021, `athena`)** installs differently. There's no LineageOS for it: after the saiyaku-athena unlock, `tools/install-athena.py` puts TECHO5's own 64-bit mainline kernel and the system on it from TWRP, backing up every partition first. Three of the screen panels Amazon used are tested on that kernel; the installer checks yours, and others install with `--force-panel`. An opt-in boot layer falls back to the other slot by itself if a new kernel doesn't start. Every step: **[docs/install-athena.md](docs/install-athena.md)**. The story and the hardware: [TECHO5 ATHENA](https://github.com/HuskerMinion/techo5-athena). **Skylight Calendar 15 (150-CAL)** isn't an Echo and needs no unlock. On its stock firmware (D156.V1.3) adb is open, and `tools/install-skylight.py` backs up the whole eMMC, then puts TECHO5's own 64-bit mainline kernel and the system on it. The installer knows that one firmware and refuses any other. It has been tried on one unit, and the way back in Loader mode hasn't been tried yet, so keep the backup. Every step: **[docs/install-skylight.md](docs/install-skylight.md)**. The older route: the daemon beside LineageOS (Windows, PowerShell) Before the Linux image, the daemon ran as an init service on LineageOS 18.1. That still works, on a unit with USB debugging and rooted debugging enabled: ```powershell cd echod $env:GOOS='linux'; $env:GOARCH='arm'; $env:GOARM='7'; $env:CGO_ENABLED='0' go build -trimpath -ldflags '-s -w' -o ../bin/echod-arm ./cmd/echod cd .. .\tools\install-cronos.ps1 -Serial -Name "Kitchen" -KeyFile .\kitchen.psk ``` The installer puts the daemon in place as an init service, switches Android to its null audio HAL (the daemon owns the microphone and speaker), provisions the name, API key and wake word models, and reboots. Home Assistant then discovers the device as an ESPHome node; paste the key when asked. Android and any app on the screen keep running, silently.
